title: Exegesis of Proverbs
english: Opposites are used: light and darkness, life and death, sickness and health; and again, falsehood and truth are named; and many other names the Scripture assigns according to the soul and its thoughts. As for what it assigns to the soul, to say but a few of many, these are: mind, soul, heart, man, man (male), woman, slave, servant, father, son, spirit, eye, mouth, lips, tongue, larynx, belly, womb, arm, finger, wood, nostril, sheep, ram, shepherd, and there are many more names of the soul, which cannot now be set forth due to the kind of commentaries that do not permit long-windedness.

Here, then, a righteous mind falls before Satan, having received an impure thought or a false dogma. And David says: 'All who descend to the earth shall fall before him' (Psalm 140:5). But this fall contains true knowledge and pure thoughts. Thus, a man who does nothing by design: 'Will' here means the inclination of the heart toward the better. 'A whip for the horse, a goad for the ox, and a rod for the fool' (Proverbs 26:3). The rod is now a symbol of punishment. He who sends a word through a foolish messenger makes a dream out of his own feet: 'Do not give holy things to dogs, nor cast pearls before swine' (Matthew 7:6). Removing the path of the legs and the proverb from the mouth of fools: 'Remove the evil path of the fool, and make a long distance of false knowledge from him.' He who releases a stone from a sling is like one giving glory to a fool: 'Knowledge does not suit a fool, and a stone is worthless in a golden sling' (Proverbs 26:11).

Much is frozen in the flesh of fools, for their ecstasy is crushed: If the ecstasy of fools, by which they were beside themselves of God, is crushed, they become pure again and approach God; for all flesh shall see the salvation of God (Luke 18:42). One must note here that he names the thickened souls from the evil flesh of fools; so also the Lord says: 'My Spirit shall not remain in these men, because they are flesh' (Psalm 51:11). Just as a dog, when it falls upon its own vomit and becomes loathsome, so a fool, turning away by his own wickedness...
Having cast his wickedness and turned again to it, he is like a dog eating his own vomit (Proverbs 26:11). A lazy man, having hidden his hand in his bosom, is unable to bring it forward.

If a tree of life is nourished from the fruits of righteousness, everyone who hides righteousness with unrighteousness will not eat from this tree. Just as one who holds a dog's muzzle, so is the one presiding over an alien judgment. Use this saying for those deciding certain unworthy ones in the sanctuary or by lot. Where there is no wrath, a battle will be stilled: He said, 'The wrathful man is a hothead' (Proverbs 25:20/14:30).

Smooth lips cover a wicked heart (Proverbs 14:30): Sorrow will not seize a pure heart, for it has driven away corrupt desires from it. If the enemy entreats you with a loud voice, do not be persuaded by him: Satan sometimes entreats us, tickling us through impure thoughts and spreading himself over us with the smoothness of pleasure, and sometimes he puts forth a voice so loud as if having been defeated, as if one should not be persuaded by one having unmitigated war against us.

For there are seven evils in his heart: These evils oppose the seven spirits. A soul being in abundance plays with masters, but a soul in want finds even bitter things sweet: A pure soul enjoys knowledge; but an impure soul considers false knowledge to be true knowledge.

Thus a man is enslaved when he is made a stranger from his own places: The place of the heart is virtue and knowledge, from which, having been made a stranger, a man falls into wickedness and ignorance and becomes a slave; because everyone who does sin is a slave of sin (John 8:34). A heart delights in myrrh, wine, and incenses: An impassive mind delights in manifold wisdom; but a passionate mind falls into ignorances.

Do not abandon your friend and your brotherly friend (Proverbs 17:17): They abandoned me, the fountain of living water (Jeremiah 2:13), and they dug pits for themselves. If you do not enter into your brother's house in misfortune: Such was the one who entered the wedding feasts and did not have wedding clothes (Matthew 22:11). A near friend is better than a brother living far away (Proverbs 18:24): Better is the one joined to me through true knowledge than the one joined to me through untrue knowledge. Having taken off his garment, for the insolent man passed away: This is the...

title: Knowledge, Law, and the Soul
english: Regarding what is said in the Gospel, 'even from him who does not have, that which he seems to have will be taken away' (Matt 25:29). This signifies, in my opinion, the intellectual remnants of virtues and the knowledge of God, which are taken from men who have used them badly.

'He who plants a fig tree shall eat its fruits' (Prov 24:13): Our Lord is the fig tree, for its fruit heals leprosy. 'If one dishonors a fool in the midst of a sitting, you will not take away his foolishness from him' (Prov 26:4-5): Not dishonoring the fool will not remove him from foolishness, but rather teaching him what kind of dishonor foolishness becomes to a stranger.

'Knowingly shepherd your souls' (Heb 13:17): Attend to yourself and direct your virtues, for men do not always remain equally strong in them; nor do they transition healthily from virtue to virtue or from knowledge to knowledge, [those] not easily receiving the human condition...; for he says 'generations' regarding virtues and knowledges, according to which the saints are born, and he shows this through what he writes: 'A generation of wisdom: the fear of the Lord, and riches, and glory, and life' (Prov 24:13-14).

This proverb should also be used toward the shepherds of the churches, to whom it is necessary to attend not to faces but to hearts, and to shepherd the sheep intellectually. 'Tend the green things in the field and shear the wool' (Song of Sol 2:16/4:16): He calls the mind a field, and the green things are the virtues existing within it by potentiality; the one tending them shears the wool, which is a symbol of the knowledge of God, which he also again calls a mountain pasture; for a mountain pasture is the knowledge of the holy powers, fitting the more irrational state of souls. It is the custom of Scripture to call the saints 'mountains.' Thus also David lifts his soul up to the mountains, whence his help shall come (Ps 121:1); and again, 'the mountains like rams, and the bulls like lambs of the flock, for the salvation of Israel' (Ps 98:7); for if angels rejoice over one repentant person, how much more over a multitude traveling from evil toward virtue. Therefore also...

Only the knowledge of the holy angels nourishes the virtues within us, from which the soul's organs of compassion are clothed: kindness, patience, humility, faith, self-control, love, and the good things born from these. For since the fields are also [metaphorical], and David speaks of rational souls, it is to be learned from here. For they say, 'Your fields shall indeed be filled with plenty' (Psalm 65:13); and again shortly after, 'And the barns shall be full of corn' (Psalm 65:14); they shall cry out, for they shall indeed sing (Psalm 96:11). For hymn and cry alone are suited to belong to rational nature.

A man who slanders the poor in impieties: If he is brave in impieties, he is brave also in virtues; and if the brave man slanders the poor in impieties, the brave man in virtues exhorts the poor; surely everyone who exhorts the poor is brave in pieties. But those who love the law surround themselves with a wall: Everyone who loves the law practices the law, and everyone who practices the law acquires apathy and knowledge of God; if then those who love the law surround themselves with a wall, now the wall signifies apathy and the knowledge of God, which alone is suited to guard the rational nature.

He who shepherds profligacy dishonors his father: He calls the mind a shepherd, and the passions within it are sheep, which he nourishes within himself through the transgression of the law, thereby dishonoring God; for profligacy is a sickness of the soul, consisting of passionate thoughts carried out through the body; but profligacy of the mind is the assumption of false dogmas and theories.

He who increases his wealth through usury and abundance brings it to the one who shows mercy to the poor: If the wealth of the impious is wickedness, and wise men will destroy it, it is evident that the righteous and wise are destroying wickedness by leading the impure toward virtue through spiritual teaching. He who turns his ear not to hear the law, he himself has detested his prayer: It is not the law that is detested by anyone.

title: The Twelve Thrones and the Perishing of the Ungodly
english: Prayer, but God is the one who gave the law. And Paul says: 'The Scripture foretells what is to come' (Rom 5:2), instead of 'The one who gave the Scripture.' He who explains and reproves will be loved. I said: I will confess my lawlessness to the Lord, and you have forgiven the impiety of my heart.

A lion hungry and a wolf thirsty, who tyrannizes being a poor man of a meager nation: If those who hunger and thirst for righteousness are blessed (Matt 5:6), those who hunger and thirst for injustice are lions and wolves. A king in need is a great slanderer: The approaches of the evil king are evils and false doctrines; for those ruled by him approach these things to him.

A man who guarantees a murderer will be a fugitive and not in safety: He who guarantees Satan guarantees injustice, promising to him that he will render the fruits of injustice. And concerning this the Gospel also says as one defiled through murder and sedition was cast into prison (Acts 25:11). A lawless nation shall by no means obey: The lawless nation is the order of the demons, to which the educated son does not obey.

He who works his own land will be filled with bread: He who cleanses himself will be filled with knowledge, but the unclean will be filled with ignorance. He who is ashamed of the faces of the unrighteous is not good: If the virtues are the faces of the righteous, he is not good who is not ashamed of the virtues; and if evils are the faces of sinners, he is good who is not ashamed of the evils. An insolent man hastens to be rich: Therefore the merciful in the age to come, having been shown mercy by God and having become angels, shall rule over the ungodly. Such is the status and...

He promised his disciples that the Lord would give them to sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. A throne is that in which the mind sits, a spiritual knowledge, gathering together those who have wandered from godliness. And to judge there means to teach, as 'Open your mouth with the word of God and judge all things healthily' (Ps 89:8), instead of 'Teach.' It is also necessary to know this: that the merciful one, having grasped the staff, himself will not become a staff, but will rather make the staff merciful.

And in the destruction of those, the righteous will be multiplied: If the ungodly perish in being ungodly, they will become righteous; for destruction now means the removal of ungodliness. Thus also Matthew, the tax collector (Matt 9:9), having been lost, the Lord granted him righteousness. For when it is burning, there is no healing (Matt 13:12): He did not say that once the flame has ceased there is no healing, but that while it is burning there is no healing, as one still having clearly wood, hay, or straw (Matt 13:12); if even for those being burned, health is found to approach after the ember.

And when ungodly rulers prevail, men groan: All those who are under the rulers and the authorities and the cosmic rulers of this darkness (Eph 6:12), all these groan. He who pastures prostitutes, destroys wealth: He who nurtures wickedness destroys wealth.

—Otherwise. A shepherd is a good mind having acquired passionless thoughts; and a shepherd is an evil mind having acquired passionate thoughts. If this is so, then surely a passionate thought is a goat, and a passionless thought is a sheep; therefore also the Lord stands the goats on the left and the sheep on the right (Matt 25:32-33); and he calls them both goats and sheep...

title: Discipline, Pride, and the Law
english: Those having sheep and goats, that is, those possessing passions and impasses. Thus also he brought forward those having weeds and those having grain having grain, naming them according to the best and worst skill. Such is also what is said by Paul, 'Love does not fail' (1 Cor 13:8), instead of 'He who has love.' A righteous king raises up a land: Christ raises up the rational nature, but the antichrist undermines it. And to a poor man there is no discerning mind: surely he is poor who does not have a discerning mind.

And a foolish man being angry is laughed at and does not fall: 'And upon him, says David, they will laugh and say, Behold a man who did not set God as his helper' (Ps 35:16; Ps 36:14). Men of blood hate the holy, but the upright seek its soul: this one seeks the soul of a righteous man, he who wishes to understand things as they have been thought. A wise man is stored up by parts: this one stores up his passion by parts, namely, he who is angry at things toward the righteous, or he who consumes his passion by parts through long-suffering; and toward the simple one the former should be spoken, but toward the diligent the latter.

There shall not be an interpreter for the nations to the lawless: to those who have kept the law there shall be an interpreter; but to those who have acted lawlessly, an interpreter there shall not be, but a punisher shall be; if indeed not a word but a rod is given to the lawless for the nations. A hard servant will not be instructed by words: because no one is hard by nature, it demonstrates, 'For even if he should understand, he will not obey' (Exod 7:22); for he who is hard by nature would never understand anything right. I say this because of Pharaoh the hard...

Having been set upon Israel, and having been disciplined not by words but by beating. He who squanders shall be a servant from childhood. If squandering makes one sin, and everyone doing the sin is a slave to sin, then everyone who squanders is a slave to sin.

Pride humbles a man: Now he calls the wickedness of the rational soul 'pride'. He who divides with a thief hates his own soul: The thief, he says, does not come except to steal and to sacrifice and to destroy. If, after an oath is proposed, hearing them do not announce: He spoke an oath according to the law; for just as the oath sets God in the soul, so also the law introduces God into the soul; and in whatever way perjury again removes God from the soul, so also lawlessness casts God out of it. If, therefore, he says, having heard the law being set, they do not confess their sins, having feared and been ashamed of men, they shall be tripped up.

So also David: 'I have sworn and I have stood to keep the judgments of your righteousness' (Ps 119:76). And again Solomon says: 'He who covers his impiety shall not prosper, but he who explains and reproves shall be loved.' And David said, he says: 'I said, I will confess my lawlessness to the Lord, and you forgave the impiety of my heart' (Ps 32:5). And 'Say, you first, your lawlessness.'

Many heal the faces of leaders: In doing what is right we heal the angels; for they themselves are the leaders of us, having taken us from the beginning, when the Most High divided the nations and set the borders of the nations according to the number of his angels. And that which is just from the judgment shall be for us from the Lord on that day, when he judges the inhabited world in righteousness; if indeed all the judgment

title: Clothing and Symbols of the Soul
english: The father has given to the son. What woman will find a brave one? Bravery is an excellent state of the rational soul, by which it has mastered the opposing forces of enemies. Such a thing will not be despoiled by dogs: having conquered the opposing power, we plunder it, learning the discourses concerning it.

Wool and linen being dyed: the soul is dyed like wool and linen, exercising itself in the discourses concerning the living and the non-living, or examining the discourses concerning the practical and the natural. And someone said that the soul is dyed like wool and linen, pulling the contemplation of bodies and incorporeal things toward it through the practical life.

And rising from the nights, she gave food to the household: the one who practices righteousness finds the soul rising from the night, being watchful; and certainly, also praying so that she might not fall into temptation; for she herself hastens to say, 'I awoke and became like a sparrow perching on a roof' (Ps 84:3). And her lamp is not extinguished through the whole night: a pure mind is a lamp, filled with spiritual contemplation. Her wicks are set in a lampstand: a pure mind is a lampstand, weaving virtue with virtue and doctrine with doctrine; or an articulated word, drawing spiritual contemplation from the mind.

Her husband does not care for those in the house when he lingers: the mind would not go forth, nor would it come to be in the contemplation of the incorporeal, without first correcting what is within; for the disturbance of the domestic affairs is accustomed to turn it back toward those from which it had departed; having acquired impassibility, it will linger in contemplation, and will not care for those in the house; for the passion is indeed [clothed in] practical and humble...
Wisdom, but desire [requires] temperance and self-control. Clothing itself of deep color and purple: The words of earth and sea are garments of the rational soul from the depths and the purple.

Another will say that the contemplation of events and the contemplation of the Holy Trinity are the clothing of a pure mind from the depths and the purple. He made linen cloths and gave them, but belts to the Canaanites (Mark 2:22): The linen cloth revealed on the roof (Mark 2:9) was a symbol of this sensible world; for the various animals contained therein showed the diverse characters of men, having been purified by the cross of Christ. If one linen cloth signified this world, perhaps many linen cloths contain the contemplation of various worlds, which the pure soul having contemplated, shared with others. If the Canaanites are interpreted as the lowly, it was not rightly that he gave the linen cloths to the lowly in mind, but rather the linen cloths to the pure, and to the Canaanites belts, which are symbols of practice, binding the passionate part of the soul.

Secure dwellings of its house: If the devil is king of all those in the waters and finds no rest through dry places, it is rightly said that the dwellings of the pure soul are secure. And he did not eat lazy grain: They say lazy grain is the grain of wickedness. For a prudent woman is blessed (Proverbs 31:30), but let this one praise the fear of the Lord (Psalm 111:10): If the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, the soul which happens to possess wisdom rightly praises the fear of the Lord, which has become to her a precursor of such knowledge.
They were collected from which we found them spread out. And again, these were corrected by the hands of Pamphilus and Eusebius.
